name: Storage Access API (for embedded SSO)
plain: Lets an embedded iframe ask for its own cookies back on third party pages.
meaning: Restores a login cookie inside an embed with a browser prompt. Used for SSO widgets and embedded apps.

access.prompt_ui: Browser prompt to let embedded site use cookies on the host site
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

story.what_it_is: An embedded widget on another site can ask to get its own cookies back.

marketing.name: Storage Access API
marketing.pitch: WebKit introduced it so embedded content can ask for cookie access after a person interacts, instead of tracking by default.

marketing.name: Storage Access API
marketing.pitch: Describes how an embedded frame can request access to its own cookies, usually after a click and sometimes a prompt.

story.for_you: A small box appears over an embedded sign in or comment widget asking if the site can use its saved cookies. You may also be asked to click inside the widget first. If you say no, the widget asks you to sign in again.
story.for_makers: Browsers block third party cookies, which breaks embedded logins, comments, video players and chat. This API lets those widgets work again with consent, so a single sign on box inside another site still recognizes the person.

use_cases.example: A video site embeds a player on a partner page and asks for access so a subscriber is recognized and ads are skipped.
A comment or like widget on a news site asks to use its cookies so a person's account shows without signing in again.
A shared office app embedded inside another tool needs it to open the same signed in workspace.
A game embedded on a portal site uses it to keep a player signed in to the game publisher's account.
A payment or login iframe asks for its cookies so a saved card stays available.
Ad and measurement frames also ask for cookies, so browsers show a prompt and block the request unless the person interacts.

risks: Embedded party can track you across sites

technical_bounds: Only the cookie jar of the embedded origin
Safari asks for prior first party interaction

history.change: Storage Access API ships in Safari
